help.intro: A report is one reader accusing one article or comment of something. Nothing here files them — readers do, from the public site — and nothing here rewrites them: the text is their accusation, and this screen is only what happens next.
help.step_1_body: Reporting requires an account, so every row carries a name you can ask about it. One live report per person per target, which is what makes the reporter count meaningful rather than a measure of how often someone clicked.
help.step_2_title: Read the reason, then the target
help.step_2_body: The reason is the report; the description is optional and often empty, which is fine. Only articles and comments can be reported — a review is dealt with by flagging it in moderation instead.
help.step_3_body: Resolving stamps the decision with your name and the time; reopening clears both, because a moderator's name on an undecided report reads as a decision. Once resolved, the reporter can no longer amend or withdraw it — the row is the record the decision is answered from.
help.step_4_title: Watch the count, not the single report
help.step_4_body: Three separate people reporting the same comment flag it automatically and take it out of the thread until someone looks. Reports on an article only ever land here — nothing is hidden on their account.
help.step_5_body: Open reports are the default view. Filter by target, reason, reporter or the moderator who closed it; search matches the description only, so a report with no text is reachable by filter alone.
help.note: Dismissing a report is a soft delete and can be restored, but it also frees that reader's slot on the target — so they may file a fresh one, and restoring the old one then collides with it. Reports on a comment disappear with the comment; reports on an article survive its deletion, because an article can come back.
